# Session 1 — charge nurse, day shift (synthetic)

Interviewer: Walk me through how you track bed status during a shift.
Karen Voss: Honestly? A paper sheet on a clipboard. The system board lags — sometimes forty minutes behind. Last Tuesday, March 14, we nearly assigned two patients to the same room on the Dayton campus.
Interviewer: What happens when the board lags?
Karen Voss: I call the unit clerk. If she's at lunch I page Dr. Patel's team directly, which they hate. For one patient — MRN 4471892 — I had three different statuses in three systems.
Interviewer: How do handoffs work at shift change?
Karen Voss: Fifteen minutes, verbal, from memory. The off-going nurse reads from her own notes. Stuff falls through — diet orders, pending transports. I keep my cell on me, the float pool texts me at 555-0182 because the paging system needs a desktop login.
Interviewer: If you could fix one thing?
Karen Voss: One screen that's actually current. I don't need predictions, I need the truth about right now.
